verdict:
The gate analysis holds pin by pin on its main claims, with five exceptions listed below. I checked the equations against TR:25-27. I checked the 5-package realisation against the generator's pinout helpers (gen/netlist.py:41-53 for lvc2g and lvc1g11, and the U105 entry at :175-177). I checked the comparator POR states (D B.7, about line 1866) and the EIB fail-safe chain (D:1797-1806, gen/netlist.py:243-285). The pin numbers, the package count (11 to 5), the POR behaviour of the SAFETY-1 term and the ribbon-open rows are correct.

- During comparator POR, U119 FCC_OFF reads LOW, so FCCNN = 1. U120 FCC_ON also reads LOW, so FCCP = 0.
- The analysis is also right that the D:1836 B.6 row is wrong. With ribbon 8 open, R270 pulls U202 A LOW, U202 Y floats, R252 turns Q201 on, and the input stays held.

The SAFETY-1 finding is valid. However, it is not the only latent single fault that releases the converter. Any stuck-HIGH output in the gate chain (U118A H1U, U118B FCCP, U110A GATE, U110B ILIM_REL) has the same effect. Nothing reads these outputs back now that U203 and pin 33 are gone. The SAFETY-1 fix therefore hardens one input of a chain whose gates have no protection.

The SAFETY-2 functional check, as proposed, is probably insensitive. It would also create a short R3 violation while the fault it tests for is present. CE_DRV now comes straight from pin 5, with no ARM_OK heartbeat gate and no push-pull buffer. Two cases follow from that and were missed: a 4-5 ribbon short while pin 5 is high-Z, and the reset-default pad keeper.

Confidence: high on the netlist and pinout facts and on the divider arithmetic. Medium on the BQ25798 timing behaviour behind the SAFETY-2 critique, which I did not verify in SLUSDV2C. I did not check whether the fabricated EIB is already populated.
errors: The SAFETY-1 hazard is described as unique to U120. It is not. In r8, the U203 far-end ILIM sense caught any CR-side output stuck HIGH (FR-08(a), pin 33; D B.6, about line 1825; gen/netlist.py:270-274). The reduced gate removes that sense. Each of these single latent faults now releases ILIM_HIZ in regen-armed cruise with BT on the bus and /CE LOW: U118A 1Y (H1U), U118B 2Y (FCCP), U110A 1Y (GATE), U110B 2Y (ILIM_REL), or a short of the ILIM_REL net to 3V3. Pin 34 reads back only the raw comparator output H1 (R126, gen/netlist.py:194), not H1U or GATE. The FCC_ON AND NOT FCC_OFF fix covers the comparator and leaves every gate output exposed. This should be stated as a J.1 accepted risk or as a T-C-05 build test. Without that, SAFETY-1 alone suggests a coverage the gate does not have.

The analysis says 'ILIM_REL_A/B' gives a two-switch release. It gives independence only on the EIB. Both ILIM_REL_A (R131A) and ILIM_REL_B (R131B) hang on the single CR net ILIM_REL (gen/netlist.py:200-201), which one gate output drives (U110B in the new mapping). A single CR-side fault therefore opens both EIB switches, Q203 (the feed) and Q201 (the hold). In r8 this was also true (U114B), but U203 detected it. The analysis does not mention that this common-mode fault is now undetected.

The SAFETY-2 fix, writing EN_CHG = 1 for at most 5 ms during qualification and expecting no charge, is probably insensitive and also unsafe under the fault. During qualification QF = 1 and the converter is released. If /CE really is stuck LOW, the test enables charging from VBUS in Run. That is the R3' violation the test is meant to rule out, even if brief. The BQ25798 charge start (converter soft start, then the charge state machine) and the CHG_STAT/IBAT ADC update are very likely slower than 5 ms, so IBAT would read about 0 and CHG_STAT would read 'not charging' even with /CE LOW. The test would then pass a faulty board. TODO(verify: SLUSDV2C, charge start latency and the REG1C/ADC update rate). An alternative within the operator's stance: on the already-fabricated EIB, keep U204 and its divider fitted as a build-time-only check, probed at J201.13 in T-C-05, with no Teensy pin.

The SAFETY-2 cause list is stale for the proposed EIB. It cites D:1843-1845, where 'R272 and R272b both open' pulls /CE toward 0 V through R263. The analysis itself proposes R258-R265 as DNP. With R263 not fitted, that double-open fault leaves /CE FLOATING, not LOW. SLUSDV2C (pin table, quoted at D:1798) says /CE must not float, so the charger's behaviour is undefined rather than 'charge allowed'. The row needs restating.
missed_cases: Ribbon 4-5 short with pin 5 high-Z (MCU reset, bootloader or flashing, or pin 5 left as an INPUT). In r8, U114 drove CE_DRV push-pull and held it LOW whenever ARM_OK = 0. Now only R108 47k (CR) and R267 47k (EIB, behind R250 1k) pull CE_DRV_J down. The STAT pull-up R107 10k to 3V3 (gen/netlist.py:213) reaches CE_DRV_J through the short (STAT high-Z: the charger is not charging or is unpowered). The Thevenin estimate is 3.3 x 23.8k / (23.8k + 10k) = about 2.32 V on the ribbon, about 2.27 V at U201 1A. That is above VIH 2.0 V, so /CE goes LOW. The D.3 claim 'LOW or high-Z = inhibited' (TR section 4, row 5) then fails. The consequence is mostly moot in reset, because the RT1987 EN pull-downs leave the charger unpowered. However, the B.6 short table row 4-5 (D, about line 1849) assumes a push-pull CE_DRV and must be re-derived. Possible fix: lower R108 to 10k (the divider then gives about 1.3 V), or keep a buffer.

The pad keeper on pins 5 and 10. D FR-01 (line 2966) records the i.MX RT1062 reset pad state as PKE = 1 / PUE = 0, a keeper (IMXRT1060RM section 11.6.191). Pin 5 (CHG_ARM, now driving /CE directly) and pin 10 (CHG_QUAL, now a level release with no one-shot) previously reached the charger only through the ARM_OK heartbeat gate or the U111 edge-triggered one-shot. Now a keeper holding either pin HIGH through a reset or boot is opposed only by a 47k pull-down. Keeper strength is TODO(verify: IMXRT1060RM). FR-49 checks the pad setting of pins 27-32 only (D:3015). Recommend extending FR-49 to pins 5 and 10, and adding both to T-D-01.

Pin 10 (QUAL) is the Teensy 4.1 default SPI CS0 (LPSPI4_PCS0). The MDAC uses SPI on pins 11-13 with chip selects on 36/37. If any library or the core claims pin 10 as the hardware CS, QUAL becomes a pulsing level. Under r8 the edge-triggered one-shot (CLR = P5N) bounded that. Now QF = QUAL AND FCCN AND P5N follows it directly whenever P5 is LOW and FCC is off. That state includes Run with P5 LOW, for example the FR-47(a) pack-OV inhibit while regen is armed, where the release then holds with /CE HIGH as the only barrier. TODO(verify: Teensy SPI library and core pin 10 claim); add a host test.

U119 FCC_OFF stuck HIGH (it falsely reads 'proven off') is not enumerated. Under the reduced gate without SAFETY-1, it forces RFC_OFF = 1 in every FC window. That gives the regen clamp of 1.33-1.76 A instead of the FC clamp of 0.65-0.95 A (D B.6 ILIM levels). The FC image register, FR-09 and OC_FC still bound it, and it is undetected. With the SAFETY-1 term, FCCNN = 0 instead disables FC charging, a safe and self-announcing failure. This case is an extra argument for the SAFETY-1 fix and should go in its rationale.

J101.11 and J101.13 tied to GND, against the EIB that is already fabricated (fab/eib_2026-11-11). If that EIB is already populated with U203 and U204, DNP is no longer an option. U203 then drives R265 470 ohm into GND at about 7 mA, which is inside the 10 mA output short-circuit limit of the r4 finding (D, about line 1825), so it is safe but wasted. U204 likewise. Those R262/R263 still load /CE as accounted in H.19. Leaving J101.11/.13 not connected avoids the question. The r5 adjacent-pair table also changes: a 10-11 short now drives RFC_OFF (U106B through R132 100 ohm) into a hard GND at about 33 mA. That is above the LVC recommended IOL/IOH of 24 mA at 3.0 V, though within the 50 mA absolute maximum. TODO(verify: SCES201N). The pair fails safe (FC clamp), but the short-table row must be re-derived.

The edge-rate exception moves. The T-D-01 fallback (D:1697, Schmitt buffers on CHG_ARM) assumed CHG_ARM fed only CR logic. Now the slow pin-5 fall goes straight down the 0.30 m ribbon into U201 1A, and the slow QUAL fall goes into a plain U107 input instead of the U111 Schmitt B input. Both chatter only toward the safe state while the other inputs hold, so this is not an R3' breach. However, the fallback must now buffer pin 5 before R130 and pin 10 before U107, and T-D-01 must scope /CE at the EVM, not only ILIM_REL.

Hang or stall in Run with P5 LOW and QUAL stuck HIGH (pin 10 fault, or a T10 conductor shorted to the adjacent T6 3V3 conductor in the new 10-cavity J-TAP; the cavity order is TODO(verify: dec-leads)). This releases the converter indefinitely with /CE HIGH as the only barrier, in a regen-armed topology where the bus feeds VCHG-IN through MOT_PWR and REGEN. The BQ25798 then still powers SYS from VBUS with charging disabled. TODO(verify: SLUSDV2C NVDC behaviour with /CE HIGH). Accepted cost 6 in TR covers firmware dropping pin 10, but not a hardware stuck-HIGH. Combined with SAFETY-2 (/CE stuck LOW), this is a two-fault R3 breach with both faults latent.
